answer: Sybil resistance here is a live-host duty. At join, an account seals a unique token to one machine and records that binding under a public shale of identity maps. Each epoch the network sends a random signal, and only the host holding that token can echo a valid proof within a tight round-trip window. One machine can present only one token at a time, and a shared proxy fails the latency fingerprint, so a farm of N names has to run N separately hosted, always-on endpoints. The operating cost therefore rises in step with every extra fake identity.
